guardrails.title: Single Responsibility
guardrails.body: Each spec shall address one concern. Do not bundle unrelated changes into a single specification. When a user creates an Issue or request, it defines the scope boundary for a single spec. The AI shall not propose splitting a user-defined Issue into multiple specs. Whether an Issue constitutes one concern is the user's judgment.

guardrails.title: Task Single Responsibility
guardrails.body: Each task within a spec shall address one concern. A task whose title or goal connects unrelated actions (e.g. 'Add X and refactor Y' where X and Y have no shared concern) shall be split. Tasks whose acceptance criteria or implementation_notes span unrelated modules without a shared concern shall be split.

guardrails.title: Unambiguous Requirements
guardrails.body: Requirements shall avoid vague adjectives (e.g. "appropriate", "fast", "easy") and instead state verifiable conditions.

guardrails.title: Complete Context
guardrails.body: Each requirement shall be specific enough that two independent reviewers would agree on whether an implementation satisfies it. Requirements using subjective terms (e.g. 'improve', 'clean up', 'optimize') without measurable criteria shall be rewritten.

guardrails.title: Requirement Verification Criteria
guardrails.body: At the Spec stage, each requirement shall state what will be checked, how it will be checked, and the observable expected result that determines whether the requirement is satisfied. For testable behavior, define the relevant input or conditions and expected outcome; for requirements not verifiable by automated tests, define a concrete inspection method and acceptance condition. Rewrite vague goals, unsupported future guarantees, and unspecified verification methods into checkable conditions. Evaluate the specification's verification plan and acceptance conditions, not whether implementation or test execution has already occurred. Implementation diffs, test code, and test execution results belong to later stages; their absence at the Spec stage is not a violation of this rule.

guardrails.title: No Hardcoded Secrets
guardrails.body: Source code shall not contain API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets directly. Externalize them via environment variables or configuration files.

guardrails.title: No Silent Error Swallowing
guardrails.body: Empty catch blocks or code that silently discards errors are prohibited. Errors shall be logged or re-thrown.

guardrails.title: Prioritize Requirements
guardrails.body: When requirements number more than three items, assign each requirement one priority: must, should, or nice-to-have.

guardrails.title: Impact on Existing Features
guardrails.body: Changes shall list their impact on existing features. If no existing features are affected, state so explicitly.

guardrails.title: Migration Parity
guardrails.body:
When a change moves, splits, extracts, replaces, or externalizes existing behavior, the draft/spec shall define migration parity before implementation. It shall inventory the existing public behavior being moved or replaced; list affected user-facing commands, APIs, hooks, config entries, generated artifacts, and side effects; map each retained behavior to its new owner or an explicit decision to remove it; define acceptance criteria proving retained behavior still works through the new path; and include at least one behavior-level verification for each retained public surface. Registration, discovery, help output, or mock routing alone are not sufficient evidence of migration parity. Intentional behavior removal shall state the user-visible impact and compatibility expectation.

Violation: missing migration parity definition
Diff-verification conditions:
- The diff moves, splits, extracts, replaces, or externalizes existing behavior.
- The draft/spec lacks an inventory of the existing public behavior being moved or replaced.
- The draft/spec lacks a mapping from each retained behavior to its new owner or an explicit removal decision.
- The draft/spec relies only on registration, discovery, help output, or mock routing checks for parity evidence.
Blocking when: retained public behavior lacks behavior-level verification through the new path, or an intentional removal lacks user-visible impact and compatibility expectations.
Advisory when: the migration inventory and mapping exist, but an additional retained surface would benefit from clearer acceptance wording without changing the implementation target.

guardrails.title: Bounded Resource Usage
guardrails.body: Recursive processing, retries, and bulk data loading shall have explicit upper bounds (depth, count, size). Designs that allow unbounded processing are prohibited. acknowledged-exception handling: when a `## Matched Spec Acknowledgment Rationale` section is present for this guardrail, an intentional exception MAY pass only if the matched rationale comes from spec.json constraints, clarifications, or alternatives_considered, includes this guardrail_id at least once, and contains at least 20 non-whitespace characters after removing the guardrail_id. Example: `bounded-resource-usage` is acknowledged because the prompt section caps entries per guardrail, characters per entry, and total section size.

guardrails.title: No Sensitive Data in Logs
guardrails.body: Logs shall not contain passwords, tokens, or personally identifiable information. Sensitive data shall be masked or excluded.

guardrails.title: No Disabling Existing Tests
guardrails.body: **CRITICAL** Skipping, commenting out, or deleting existing tests to make them pass is prohibited. When tests fail, fix the product code. MUST NOT bypass failing tests by disabling them. If the feature under test is itself deleted, deleting the corresponding tests is justified.

guardrails.title: Spec Includes Test Strategy
guardrails.body: The spec shall include a test strategy (what to test and how).

guardrails.title: Present Recommendations with Reasoning
guardrails.body: For each question, present a recommended answer. State the basis: (1) project docs/, (2) guardrail principles, or (3) existing code patterns. Lead with the recommendation and keep it concise.

guardrails.title: Explore Before Asking
guardrails.body: If a question can be answered by reading docs/ or exploring the codebase, do so before asking the user.

guardrails.title: Proactively Raise Related Implications
guardrails.body: When a decision has obvious related implications, raise them proactively. Do not wait for the user to notice the gap.

guardrails.title: Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing
guardrails.body: Before critiquing a decision, confirm whether the user is brainstorming or deciding. Do not evaluate brainstorming ideas as final decisions.

guardrails.title: Capture Digressions in draft.md
guardrails.body: When a discussion digresses, capture key insights and decisions in draft.md before returning to the main thread.

guardrails.title: Draft Stays at Requirements Level
guardrails.body: Draft is RFP/requirements level only. Mentioning file paths or function names as context is permitted. Do not describe internal algorithms, data structures, control flow, or API design. Code references within the evidence, why, and answer fields of QA entries are provided as justification and do not constitute implementation details.

guardrails.title: Synthesize Draft, Do Not Copy
guardrails.body: Organize and abstract draft content rather than copying it directly. Do not invent content not present in the draft.

guardrails.title: Record Unresolved Points as Open Questions
guardrails.body: Place unresolved points in the Open Questions section. Do not fabricate answers.

guardrails.title: Include 'Why This Approach' Rationale
guardrails.body: The spec shall include the rationale for why this approach was chosen.

guardrails.title: Escalate Pre-Existing Test Failures
guardrails.body: If a test that was already failing before implementation is discovered, report it to the user and confirm the remediation policy. Do not independently fix test failures that were not caused by your own implementation.

guardrails.title: Spec Test Coverage
guardrails.body:
Verify that the implementation conforms to requirements and specifications. New spec behavior coverage MUST be written under specs/<specid>/tests/ with a `// spec: R<N> ...` header per file. Existing shared regression tests under tests/ MAY be updated when production contracts change, but those updates do not substitute for the required spec-local coverage. Runtime spec-local pass/fail is verified at the integration scope by test-execute and test-result-review, while full project regression is verified by final-regression before finalize; task-impl gates inspect diff and header coverage only.

Violation: a gate requires evidence owned by a later lifecycle step
Diff-verification conditions:
- The current integration gate has current PASS test-execute and test-result-review evidence for spec-local requirements.
- The spec assigns full project regression evidence to final-regression.
- final-regression is ordered after the current integration gate and remains pending.
Blocking when: current-step-owned test evidence is missing or failed, or required spec-local/shared regression coverage is absent from the diff.
Advisory when: current-step-owned evidence passes and only optional test coverage could be improved. A pending downstream final-regression step alone is neither blocking nor advisory.

guardrails.title: Project Test Integrity
guardrails.body: Ensure that implemented code continues to work after merging by adding or updating project test code as needed. All project tests MUST pass. At the task-impl gate, inspect the diff for the necessary project test changes only; do not require runtime test evidence or completion of the later test-execute and final-regression steps. Runtime pass/fail is verified by those later lifecycle owners before finalize.

guardrails.title: Code Placement
guardrails.body:
Before writing new logic, identify which existing module owns the relevant data or responsibility and place the logic there.

Violation: derivation logic placed in consumer module
Diff-verification conditions:
- The diff adds a new export or module in a consumer layer.
- The new logic operates on data owned by an existing data-owner module.
- The diff makes no change to that owner module.
Blocking when: the consumer layer now derives, queries, or decides from owner data while the owner module remains unchanged.
Advisory when: the diff only moves presentation formatting or adds a temporary adapter with explicit follow-up evidence.

guardrails.title: Avoid Overengineering
guardrails.body:
Avoid abstractions and duplication that are not justified by the diff.

Violation: single-caller indirection
Diff-verification conditions:
- The diff adds a helper, wrapper, class, or module.
- Exactly one production caller is added or remains after the change.
- The abstraction does not hide meaningful complexity or enforce an invariant.
Blocking when: the indirection adds a new API surface with no shared behavior, invariant, or ownership boundary.
Advisory when: the indirection is a small naming aid or prepares an explicitly approved follow-up.

Violation: duplicate code shape
Diff-verification conditions:
- The same statement or control-flow shape appears in two or more changed locations.
- The repeated shape performs the same transformation or decision.
- A local helper could remove the repetition without changing ownership.
Blocking when: duplicate behavior is introduced in production code.
Advisory when: the duplication is limited to tests or intentionally mirrors separate domain concepts with documented rationale.

Violation: missing design-confirmation evidence
Diff-verification conditions:
- The diff implements a non-trivial layer, data flow, or pattern choice.
- The spec or issue-log lacks evidence that the design direction was confirmed before implementation.
Blocking when: the implementation commits to a broad architecture without confirmation evidence.
Advisory when: the change is mechanically local or the confirmation evidence is present but terse.
guardrails.text: Do not introduce indirection layers that have a single caller. Prefer DRY: when the same code shape appears in two or more places, extract a helper rather than duplicating. Before implementing a non-trivial change, present the design direction (data flow, layer boundaries, chosen pattern) to the user; only proceed after confirmation.
